title: Vue components: props, events, slots, and v-model
outcome: Design a reusable component API with one owner and explicit update events.
useCase: Reusable form controls and ticket editors.
benefits: Small component contracts and testable ownership.
drawbacks: A very configurable component can become harder than two focused components.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Props describe. Events request. Slots compose.

trace.title: Owner value
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A component API is a small agreement. Props bring information in.

Events ask the owner to change something. Slots let a caller supply presentation while the component owns behavior.

Decide which part owns the saved value, draft, and focus.

Avoid mutating a nested object received as a prop. A shallow readonly prop boundary does not make every nested value immutable.

Emit an update or edit an independent draft instead.

v-model is a prop/event convention. In Vue 3.4+, defineModel is a convenience macro.

The older explicit modelValue plus update:modelValue contract is still useful to understand. Give events meaningful types and keep accidental HTML attributes from landing on the wrong element in wrapper components.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Parent changes modelValue → child renders it. User types → child emits a value → parent accepts it → new prop flows down.

This loop makes ownership visible.

For a wrapper, inspect whether id, aria-describedby, and class reach the actual input or only the wrapper div. Accessible names and error associations are part of the component’s contract.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A component that both owns a private value and blindly watches the parent prop can overwrite an in-progress edit.

A custom input without a real label is harder to use even when v-model works.
